 Former Guidance Tamil Nadu staff targeted for raising red flags? Email to CMO in August reveals tensions
 Reports claimed TVK government sacked Guidance Tamil Nadu staff for allegedly leaking data to Andhra Pradesh. Former employees that South First spoke to ask two simple question: If they were moles, why were they allowed to serve notice period and where is the evidence or action if the allegations are true. 
 Anusha Ravi Sood Published Nov 20, 2026 | 12:21 AM ⚊ Updated Nov 20, 2026 | 12:58 AM 
 Share
 Guidance Tamil Nadu is the nodal investment promotion agency of the Government of Tamil Nadu.
 -->
 Make Us Your Preferred Source on Google 
 Synopsis: Several employees resigned en masse after Deepak Jacob, IAS, took charge of Guidance Tamil Nadu as its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer. Months after they left, reports surfaced that the government had dismissed 15 employees for allegedly leaking sensitive information related to industrial investments to Andhra Pradesh. Incidentally, most of the resigned employees have taken up roles in investment promotion agencies in other states, but only those who joined Andhra Pradesh’s Economic Development Board seem to be specifically in the crosshairs. The former employees felt the allegation was meant to tarnish their professional reputation. 
 On 31 July 2026 — their last working day — an outgoing employee of Guidance Tamil Nadu emailed the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO), the Chief Secretary (CS), the Minister for Industries, and the Secretary of Industries.
 The subject line read: “ Formal complaint and threats from Mr Deepak Jacob IAS ”. South First has a copy of the email. On 1 August, 2026 a letter addressed to Chief Secretary M Sai Kumar, ‘CC’ed to Chief Minister Joseph Vijay and Dr Vijaya Kumar S, Addl CS Industries listed five issues including disrespect, unaddressed pay-parity concerns, favouritism and preferential treatment, intimidation and retaliation by MD, large-scale resignations and erosion of institutional capacity. The letter sought an independent inquiry into the preferential promotions of two employees, reviewing conduct and continuation of MD Jacob and setting up a fact-finding inquiry into the alleged threats and intimidation of employees. 
 Instead of responding to the complaint or informing them of the action being taken on the concerns raised, the complainant said four months after the email, insinuations were being made against them and 14 other former colleagues, calling them “moles who leaked data to Andhra Pradesh”.
 South First spoke to former Guidance Tamil Nadu staffers on the insinuations of leaks and moles.
 “False information is being circulated that we were ‘sacked’ when the reality is 13 out of the 15 employees resigned and, as per due process, even served a notice period. If I were leaking data, why would the government let me serve a month-long notice period? So more information could be leaked? It makes no sense,” a former employee, who exited Guidance Tamil Nadu in July 2026, told South First .
 The former employee cited a hostile work environment—after Guidance Tamil Nadu changed its Managing Director earlier this year—as the reason professionals resigned  en masse .
 “There was no clause in our employment contract restricting us from joining another Investment Promotion Agency. I, therefore, chose to leave on my own terms and pursue another professional opportunity,” the former employee added.  
 Also Read: ‘Allegations of ‘moles in Guidance TN’ 
 ‘False narratives’ 
 Many of the 15 professionals who exited Guidance in June-July this year after the TVK government came to power took up jobs in other states’ investment promotion agencies such as ‘Invest Karnataka’, ‘Invest Telangana’ and ‘Economic Development Board’ in Andhra Pradesh. But those who joined the Andhra Pradesh board have come under severe scrutiny after announcing their changed roles on their respective social media pages.
 A former employee said they left Guidance after the work atmosphere at the agency turned after Deepak Jacob took charge.
 Sections of the media on Thursday, 19 November, claimed the C Joseph Vijay-led TVK government in Tamil Nadu had identified “moles” in Guidance Tamil Nadu and “sacked 15 employees” for leaking information to Andhra Pradesh. The claims were linked to the exit of private professionals who had been employed with Guidance Tamil Nadu under the previous DMK and earlier AIADMK regimes.
 The news reports attributed the “leaks” claims to neither any minister nor any bureaucrat. Nobody from the TVK-led Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance (SSJVA) has officially, on the record, made the allegations or named any persons yet. The insinuations, however, seemed to target a few former Guidance Tamil Nadu staff who eventually took up jobs in other states — especially Andhra Pradesh.
 Former employees have once again written to the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister’s Office, Chief Secretary, Industries Minister and the secretary of the industries department, demanding action against the “false narratives” tainting their professional reputation.
 “The Tamil Nadu government has the whole machinery at its disposal to take action if these allegations of leaking information are true. Why isn’t there an FIR then? Where is the evidence? This feels like deliberate targeting of former employees for raising concerns of threats and disrespect by MD of Guidance TN Deepak Jacob,” a former employee who had worked with Guidance Tamil Nadu for five years told South First .
 The former staffer, who raised a complaint alleging intimidation and bias in August 2026, has once again written to the CMO about the distress the latest insinuations have caused and demanded a response to the earlier complaint.
 Also Read: Tamil Nadu’s big push to take local iconic food brands global 
 What was in the complaint in August? 
 The complaint mailed to the CMO, Chief Secretary and others in August alleged that certain individuals close to Industries Minister S Keerthana were favoured and given more opportunities. “ This organisation in the last 3 months has been enabling those who have personal contacts to their own benefit, and only equipping themselves,” the letter read.  
 The complaint also raised concerns of a hostile work environment after a new MD was appointed. “Others who have worked hard were treated with disrespectful words including the MD (Deepak Jacob) saying he will create a scam case against us and attack our family. We understand that this officer has been brought into Guidance with the support of Vishnu Venugopalan IAS who is now CM’s secretary protocol. This again brings a loop of friends and close connects who are benefitting from a flawed system. There has been several complaints against both officers from within the organisation as well as from the industries [sic] ,” a part of the letter read.
 The former employee insisted that they were being targeted for raising complaints against the Managing Director. They alleged that those who joined the Andhra Pradesh Economic Development Board were being dragged into the row after recent reports of investors choosing Andhra Pradesh over Tamil Nadu. 
 (Edited by Majnu Babu).
